title: Weights and SynOps
summary: A spike pushes the next neuron only as hard as the weight. Each crossing is one SynOp.

terms.definition: The strength of one connection. A spike is multiplied by this before it reaches the next neuron.
A synaptic operation: the work of delivering one spike through one weighted connection.

cards.text:
A spike does not push every neighbor the same way.
The link has a strength.

lines: Weight 0: the tip arrives and does nothing.

cards.text:
Each time one spike crosses one link, that is one synaptic operation.
The short name is SynOp.

question.prompt: Weight 3. One spike arrives. How much is added next door?
question.why: The spike is scaled by the weight. 1 × 3 = 3.
question.simpler: The spike is the event. The weight is how large that event is for this link.

question.prompt: 4 spikes each cross 5 links. How many SynOps?
question.why: Each spike meets each link once. 4 × 5 = 20.
question.simpler: Count spike-link crossings, not spikes alone.

recall.question: What is one SynOp?
recall.answer: One spike delivered through one synapse.

deeper.note: Operation counts are how SNN papers compare work to a dense network. A MAC is the dense multiply. A SynOp is the spike-driven counterpart. Roy, Jaiswal, and Panda separate those costs in their 2019 perspective.

paper.title: Towards spike-based machine intelligence with neuromorphic computing
paper.section: The sections that separate synaptic operations from dense multiplies.
